# Manage emergency access accounts: a pinned copy of Learn's alert queries

This folder is an unmodified copy of the Microsoft Learn source page for [Manage emergency access accounts in Microsoft Entra ID](https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access). It holds Microsoft's standard for emergency access accounts and the three sample Azure Monitor log queries for the alert on their use: by one object ID, by two object IDs, and by user principal name. It comes from [MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs](https://github.com/MicrosoftDocs/entra-docs/blob/07cb73d6c6380414eecd040ba5e14c1c94d48b66/docs/identity/role-based-access-control/security-emergency-access.md) at commit `07cb73d6c6380414eecd040ba5e14c1c94d48b66` (October 30, 2026); the page last changed on June 4, 2026. The repository's code license (`LICENSE-CODE`) and documentation license (`LICENSE`) are both MIT.

**Why the page, not just the queries.** The queries exist only inside this Learn page. Pinning the page byte for byte keeps the copy checkable against upstream. `examples/privileged-access/tests/LearnSampleHarness.ps1` extracts the queries, unmodified, at test time and evaluates their filters over fictional exported log rows with a small evaluator that handles only their shape (`Table | where Column == "value" or ... | project ...`). It isn't a KQL engine, and nothing is sent to a workspace. The [developer workbook *Building Privileged Access*, Chapter 02](../../../docs/project-plans/developer-workbooks/privileged-access/02-emergency-access-as-code.md) links Learn rather than quoting the page.

**How it stays honest.**

- `snapshot.json` records the upstream repository, path, commit, dates, licenses and the size and SHA-256 of every file here. Each file's git blob hash was checked against the upstream tree at that commit before the manifest was written. `scripts/tests/test_third_party_snapshots.py` fails if any file is changed, added or removed.
- The weekly source watch follows commits to the upstream page (`entra-emergency-access-page-commits` in `data/source-watch/feeds.json`) and reports each one in its issue under DW (developer workbooks).
- To move to a newer upstream commit: review the upstream change, copy the page from that commit, regenerate `snapshot.json`, rerun `examples/privileged-access/tests/MicrosoftSamples.Tests.ps1` and the Chapter 02 labs, and open a pull request. Never edit the files here; changes the program needs go in `examples/privileged-access`.

These files keep their upstream bytes, line endings included, so the hashes match the upstream commit.
